title: Cohen--Macaulayness of a scheme morphism at a point
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $x\in X$. Say that $f$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $x$ if its local ring map $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and the local ring of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_{f(x)}$ at the point corresponding to $x$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] equal to its Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Say that $f$ is Cohen--Macaulay if it is Cohen--Macaulay at every point of $X$. This explicit fibre-stalk convention agrees with Stacks Tag 045R whenever the fibres are locally Noetherian, in particular for locally finitely presented morphisms.
